what_its_for: Cyproheptadine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as runny nose, sneezing, itchy or watery eyes, and skin itching or hives. It may also be used to help stimulate appetite in some patients or to prevent migraines.
how_to_take: Take cyproheptadine exactly as your doctor or pharmacist tells you. You may take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, taking it with food or milk may help. If you are using the liquid form, carefully measure your dose with the special measuring spoon or cup that comes with the medication — do not use a regular kitchen spoon.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 4 mg taken 3 times a day. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your symptoms and how well you respond. Do not take more than 32 mg in one day unless your doctor tells you to. For children, the dose is based on weight and age, so always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store cyproheptadine at room temperature, away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Keep it out of the bathroom. Store the liquid form away from freezing temperatures — do not freeze it. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused medication safely — ask your pharmacist about the best way to do this.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication, as it can make drowsiness much worse. Be careful driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medications that cause drowsiness — such as sleep aids, anxiety medicines, narcotic pain relievers, muscle relaxers, or other antihistamines — without talking to your doctor or pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: severe drowsiness or confusion, difficulty urinating or no urination, fast or irregular heartbeat, seizures, severe dizziness, vision problems, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, severe itching, swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve or get worse.
when_it_works: Cyproheptadine usually starts working within 1 to 2 hours of taking a dose. You should begin to feel relief from allergy symptoms fairly quickly. For appetite stimulation or migraine prevention, it may take several days to weeks before you see the full benefit.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): You may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine, especially drowsiness, dizziness, confusion, and difficulty urinating. Use with caution and talk to your doctor about the right dose for you. Children: This medicine can be used in children, but the dose must be carefully determined by a doctor based on the child's weight and age. Do not give this medicine to newborns or premature babies. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as this medicine may not be safe in these situations.
